intro: Recall treats every relevant document alike. When some passages directly answer a question and others only mention the topic, use graded judgments and account for where they appear.
task: Return NDCG@k as a numeric scalar using linear relevance gains and discount log2(rank+1), where rank starts at one. Divide by the DCG of the best possible ordering of every judged document.
requirements: ranked is a Python list of nonempty string IDs. relevance is a dictionary of nonempty string IDs to finite numeric grades in [0,5]. Empty inputs are allowed.
Keep the first occurrence of each ranked ID, then take the first k. An unjudged ID has gain zero but still occupies a rank position.
k is a nonnegative Python int; bool is invalid and k may exceed the number of documents. Return zero for k=0 or ideal DCG=0.
Use grades directly, not 2**grade-1. Ideal DCG uses all relevance judgments, including documents absent from ranked. Reject malformed values with ValueError; preserve inputs.

hints.title: Retain actual rank order
hints.body: Never sort the retrieved IDs by their known grades. That would evaluate an oracle ordering rather than the system's output.

hints.title: Build a separate ideal ranking
hints.body: Sort all judgment values descending and apply the same cutoff and discount to get the denominator.

hints.title: Deduplicate before cutoff
hints.body: Keep the first occurrence using insertion order. A repeated document should not earn its gain twice.

explanation: DCG adds a relevance grade at each rank after discounting later positions. NDCG divides by an ideal score, making a perfect ordering score one when any positive judgment exists.
This lesson uses linear grades. Other implementations use exponential gains, so report the gain convention and cutoff with a metric rather than comparing differently defined numbers.

The ideal ranking includes relevant documents the system failed to retrieve. Restricting the denominator to the retrieved subset would reward omissions. This activity assigns zero to unjudged IDs; real evaluation must also examine judgment coverage.

Swap the two documents in the first example, then compare k=1 and k=2. Explain why recall at two can be unchanged while NDCG changes. A metric summarizes these judgments; it cannot prove that generated answers are factual.
formula: DCG@k = Σᵣ≤k gradeᵣ / log₂(r + 1); NDCG = DCG / ideal DCG
